items.title: Rufus Reid interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, GA, January 4, 2013
items.q: It was with the New York Bass Choir in New York... Richard Davis and Bill Lee and Lyle Atkinson.

ctx.x: I’ve been very fortunate to get to know a few of those people, like Milt Hinton. Do you have words to describe what it was like to be around him and that generation of players?

Wow. It was very fulfilling to be around him, in every way. I mean he seemed to satisfy everything you were wondering about, it was not a mystery, it was just there. He had an aura about him that was so positive, and everything was positive. I never saw him — I was around him a lot. We used to go visit him in his home when he was declining. But he still was amazing. But when he was on, you know, earlier in years he was playing, it was a true, it was just honest stuff. He wasn’t trying to show off, he just did…

said, “Well I’m going now, come on with me.” And we walked, and I had to walk faster to keep up with him. And that’s how our relationship, from that day, it was perfect. He was really, really, really wonderful.
